<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-docs.mjs from openvireo-core v1.2.2@f3ba085 + 4 docs commits to 11a2705; do not edit by hand. -->

The core is Rust, and Rust programs use it directly. Each binding exposes the same facade (`ov_core`): `OvClient`, `Account`, `Vault`,
`ServiceAccount`, `SelfHosted`, the records, `OvError` with the same codes, and the crypto, share-link
and TOTP functions. None of them reimplements OPAQUE, keysets or the KDBX merge. A program on any
binding interoperates with the apps.

| Language | Use it for | Binding | Get it | Docs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rust | Rust programs, services and tools | none: the `openvireo-core` crate itself (`ov_core`) | Cargo git dependency on a release tag | [Rust](/bindings/rust/) |
| TypeScript / JavaScript | Web apps, Node, Bun, CLIs | wasm (`bindings/ov-wasm`), wrapped by `@openvireo/sdk` | npm: `@openvireo/sdk` (or `@openvireo/core-wasm` for the low-level calls) | [SDK docs](https://developer.openvireo.com/sdk/) |
| Swift | iOS and macOS apps | UniFFI (`bindings/ov-ffi`), module `OpenVireoRustCore` | Swift Package Manager: [openvireo-swift](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-swift) | [Swift](/bindings/swift/) |
| C++ | Qt and other native desktop code | cxx (`bindings/ov-ffi-cpp`), `<ovcore.h>` | CMake package `libovcore` on each GitHub release (or Corrosion from source) | [C++](/bindings/cpp/) |
| Python | Scripts, automation, backends | UniFFI (`bindings/ov-ffi`), package `openvireo` | PyPI: `openvireo` | [Python](/bindings/python/) |
| Kotlin / Java | JVM services and tools, Android apps | UniFFI (`bindings/ov-ffi`), package `com.openvireo.core` | Maven Central: `com.openvireo:openvireo-core-jvm`, `-android` | [Kotlin and Java](/bindings/kotlin-java/) |

Pick the TypeScript SDK if you work in JavaScript. It adds a higher-level API, the `ov` CLI and the
GitHub Action on top of the core (`ov connect`, the REST server, is in the native Rust `ov`, `bins/ov`).
Use the wasm package (`@openvireo/core-wasm`) directly only for the low-level calls.

## Install

The current release of each, from its package registry. Each language's page has the details: extras,
signatures, other platforms and older releases.

```toml tab="Rust"
# Cargo.toml (not on crates.io yet)
openvireo-core = { git = "https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core", tag = "v1.2.2" }
```
```sh tab="TypeScript"
npm install @openvireo/sdk
```
```swift tab="Swift"
// Package.swift, or File > Add Package Dependencies in Xcode
.package(url: "https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-swift", from: "1.2.2")
```
```cmake tab="C++"
# FetchContent the package for your platform, with its SHA256SUMS line (see the C++ page)
FetchContent_Declare(openvireo_core URL https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/releases/download/v1.2.2/libovcore-1.2.2-<platform>.tar.gz URL_HASH SHA256=<hash>)
```
```sh tab="Python"
pip install "openvireo==1.2.2"
```
```kotlin tab="Kotlin"
// build.gradle.kts, from Maven Central
implementation("com.openvireo:openvireo-core-jvm:1.2.2")      // or openvireo-core-android
```
```xml tab="Java"
<!-- pom.xml, from Maven Central -->
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.openvireo</groupId>
  <artifactId>openvireo-core-jvm</artifactId>
  <version>1.2.2</version>
</dependency>
```

The `ov` CLI isn't a binding: it's a native program on each core release. See
[the CLI docs](https://developer.openvireo.com/cli/).

## How they differ

| | Rust | TypeScript (wasm) | Swift | C++ | Python | Kotlin / Java |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Async calls | `async` (`Send` futures, any runtime) | Promises | `async` | blocking (call from a worker thread) | asyncio coroutines | `suspend`; `CompletableFuture` in Java |
| Cancelling | `CancelToken`, or drop the future | `AbortSignal` | `CancelToken` | `CancelToken` | task cancel or `cancel=CancelToken()` | coroutine cancel or `CancelToken`; `future.cancel` in Java |
| Errors | `OvError` (`code`, `wire_code()`) | `OpenVireoError` (`code`) | `OvError` (`code`, `wireCode`) | `ov::Error` (via `ov::call`) | `OvError` (`code`, `wire_code`) | `OvException` (`code`, `wireCode`) |
| Ready-made Host | no (copy the examples' `host.rs`) | yes (fetch, IndexedDB or memory) | the app's own | the app's own | `openvireo.hosts` | `com.openvireo.core.hosts` |
| Secrets | `Vec<u8>`, caller wipes (`zeroize`) | linear memory zeroed on free | `Data`, caller wipes | `rust::Vec<uint8_t>`, caller wipes | `bytes`, can't be wiped | `ByteArray`, `fill(0)` |

## The Host

The core does no I/O. Every binding passes in a Host with five parts: an HTTP transport, a secure
store, an offline cache, a clock and a log sink. TLS, proxies, the keychain and logging stay with the
platform. [Architecture](https://github.com/openvireo/openvireo-core/blob/v1.2.2/docs/architecture.md#the-host) describes the contract. Two rules apply to every
transport: it must not follow redirects, and it must not send or store cookies.

## Versions

Every binding is built from the same commit and has the core's version, which follows SemVer:
minor releases add API, and only a major release removes or changes it. Pin an exact version.
